alternative: Use the language feature: declare one class inheriting from both parents and rely on the C3 method resolution order with cooperative super() initialisation, or hold the second provider as a collaborator and forward explicitly (thin delegating methods, or __getattr__ for a whole interface). Keep a pair of mutually referencing objects only when two independent registries must each hold their own addressable object, and then define __eq__/__hash__ on the pair and release one reference at teardown (weakref.ref where the lifetimes differ).
idiom_name: mutually referencing pair of subclasses (re-implements the multiple inheritance Python already has)
implementation_notes: Python classes already support multiple inheritance, and the method resolution order is a dynamic C3 linearisation that is monotonic and visits each diamond ancestor once 'to support cooperative calls to super()' - the tutorial's own words. Simulating that with two linked objects therefore buys nothing and costs an identity decision, a cycle and hand-written forwarding. What replaces the twin link: real multiple inheritance when both parents are Python classes (including cooperative super() initialisation), or composition with forwarding - explicit delegating methods, or __getattr__ for a whole interface - when the second provider is an object rather than a base class. The classic pair stays reasonable only for two objects that must exist separately in two registries (two collections keyed by different types) or when the second provider cannot be inherited from (a C extension object, a proxy, a remote handle); then implement __eq__/__hash__ deliberately and drop one reference at teardown.
pitfalls: Diamond shapes are resolved by linearisation rather than by the class: a base that does not cooperate (does not call super(), or calls it unconditionally) breaks initialisation - inspect Ball.__mro__ and initialise in MRO order.
Genuinely conflicting members are resolved silently in favour of the earlier class in the MRO; the class definition succeeds and the surprise appears at the call site.
Mutually referencing objects are collected by the cycle collector, but one side should still hold weakref.ref when the pair's lifetimes differ, and __del__ order is not guaranteed for cyclic garbage.
Forwarding with __getattr__ hides typos unless it raises AttributeError for unknown names, and it does not intercept special methods (len, iteration, indexing) - those must be delegated explicitly.
